kinematics.method: i = Zf/(Zc-Zf). Numeric check: wave generator stepped through one turn in 8 steps; at each step the flexspline phase that maximises the minimum CS-FS radial gap is searched; i = -Δwg/Δphase.

meshing.interference_3d: none (boolean intersection of every part pair > 1e-4 mm^3)
meshing.method: Both tooth surfaces are polar functions r(θ) (FS: Rf + w0 cos2(θ-wg) + A cos Zf(θ-φ); CS: Rc + A cos Zcθ). Gap = r_CS - r_FS sampled at 60,000 points per circle; gap > 0 everywhere means no overlap. Tooth form is a simplified cosine profile, not a production S-tooth.

flexspline_fatigue.method: Thin ring with w = w0 cos2θ: Δκ = (w''+w)/R² = -3 w0 cos2θ/R², ε = (h/2)·3w0/R². Fully reversed bending twice per wave-generator turn; cup torsion τ = T/(2π r² t) taken as steady mean stress; Goodman line. Infinite life is needed: 10^9 cycles is about 116 days of continuous running at 3000 rpm.

wave_generator_load.method: Force to spread the rim by 2·w0 across the major axis: thin ring under two diametral loads, δ = 0.149 F R³/(EI) (Roark). Tangential force F = T/Rf; about 30% of the band-overlap teeth assumed to share load.

not_covered: production tooth profile (S-tooth / IH) and tangential deflection term
